raw_text: [[File:{{{Alt}}}|28px|link=]] "Monolith Arrow's extra damage decreases when more than 180 and 250 housing spaces of units are deployed" Contents 1 Summary 2 Mechanics 3 Strategies 3.1 Offensive Strategies 3.2 Defensive Strategies 4 Statistics 5 History 6 Audio 6.1 Generic 6.2 Unique 7 Trivia 7.1 General Summary [ ] The Monolith Arrow is an Epic piece of Equipment for the Archer Queen . It was first seen in the Anime Fury Medal Event , which made its debut in June 4, 2026. The Monolith Arrow resembles a large arrow with a diamond-shaped purple tip with a glowing pink aura in the center and a light yellow base near the top of the handle. When the Monolith Arrow is equipped, the Archer Queen's attacks will deal extra damage proportional to the target's maximum hitpoints, similar to the Monolith . However, this bonus damage decreases twice, once when 181 housing space of units are deployed and once when 251 housing space is deployed. While active, the Archer Queen also takes slightly reduced damage from incoming attacks. Note that the ability damage decreases only once the described thresholds of 180 and 250 are surpassed, not when they are equalled. Thus the Monolith Arrow will still have maximum damage when exactly 180 housing space has been deployed, and will remain in its second damage stage with exactly 250 housing space deployed. Extra damage from the ability cannot be modified by damage modifications such as Rage Spells or difficulty modifiers. Every three levels, the bonus damage percentage for all three tiers is increased (by anywhere between 0.1% and 0.5%, depending on the tier); starting at level 9, the damage reduction is also increased (by 1% each time). In addition to the ability, the Monolith Arrow grants extra hitpoints to the Archer Queen. Mechanics [ ] The Monolith Arrow calculates the total amount of housing space deployed to determine its damage output, regardless of whether the Archer Queen has been deployed. This counter acts similar to the Eagle Artillery 's mechanic of activation by housing space. Attacking Heroes including the Archer Queen herself count, adding 25 housing space when they are deployed in a battle. Pets and Spells do not count. Siege Machines count as 1 housing space, however donated Siege Machines from the Clan Castle do not. Clan Castle reinforcements do not count. Subtroops such as the Witch's Skeletons , the Super Witch 's Big Boy , and the Siege Barracks ' Wizards and P.E.K.K.A (s) do not count. The Monolith Arrow counter continues to accumulate even while the Archer Queen is defeated, which may be relevant if the Queen is revived later by a Revive Spell . Strategies [ ] Offensive Strategies [ ] The Monolith Arrow is effective against high-health targets, such as the Town Hall , defending Guardians , and Walls . It can be used to trivialize battles against the Giant Dragon and M.O.M.M.A in the Single Player Campaign similarly, because it affects all units regardless of hitpoints. Upgrading it allows the Archer Queen to deal with higher-hitpoint units, therefore increasing its effectiveness. The Monolith Arrow is suited to Queen Walks and Charges, which are usually used at the start of the attack to funnel or eliminate objectives important for the rest of the attack. Such strategies do not deploy much housing space at the start, allowing the Monolith Arrow to attain its maximum potential. The Monolith Arrow is less suitable to equip if the player deploys their entire army at the start, as the maximum damage boost will be reduced significantly after deploying all of the housing spaces of the army. Defensive Strategies [ ] Most strategies from the Archer Queen, more specifically in Queen Charges, apply to this Equipment. Because the Archer Queen is commonly overwhelmed by small troops like Skeletons , the Monolith Arrow will be wasted on them, giving more time for defenses to quickly take her out before she does too much damage. Ice Golems can also do the same, as their death freeze will impede her progress in a Queen Charge, and possibly cause a time fail if the base is well-designed. Since the Archer Queen can deal bonus damage to Walls with the Monolith Arrow, so placing too few compartments can easily allow her to break through, even when the Hero Equipment is at its lowest bonus damage.
